contracts.question: What is the canonical workflow, binding and descriptor document?
contracts.decision: Separate domain workflow input/output from trigger bindings and use one versioned structural document.

contracts.question: Which values, presence rules and normalization operations are portable?
contracts.decision: Use a bounded JSON-compatible subset with explicit missing/null/default/unknown-field semantics and limits.

contracts.question: How are versioned executable artifacts made immutable and locatable?
contracts.decision: Bind execution-relevant content to deterministic digests; reject same-version content conflicts.

contracts.question: How do tools and adapters consume stable diagnostics and conformance cases?
contracts.decision: Publish versioned diagnostic/conformance records with actionable location, expected/actual and remediation fields.

contracts.question: Which typed Go authoring forms and ownership rules are supported?
contracts.decision: Applications author typed nodes and structural workflows; nodes do not import or invoke other nodes.

contracts.question: Which embedded backend provides the first durable execution implementation?
contracts.decision: Select one backend through a measured executable spike; keep the store port replaceable.

contracts.question: What persistent external-runtime protocol and topology are supported first?
contracts.decision: Node.js is first over authenticated persistent gRPC with negotiated schemas, identities, bounds and cancellation.

contracts.question: How are packages resolved, verified, locked and installed offline?
contracts.decision: E13-T01 defines immutable signed package identity/trust, validates and binds existing node/workflow schemas, carries ordinary node effects/capabilities in node.Descriptor, and accepts the existing tool.Manifest only as an explicit agent-compatible declaration. Missing manifests never imply agent eligibility; workflow documents currently have no aggregate capability field. Offline resolution, lock generation, durable cache, and atomic CLI install/update remain E13-T02–T04; language package managers are not replaced.

contracts.question: How are durable partitions fenced and work ownership transferred?
contracts.decision: Specify fencing and persistence semantics before implementing distributed admission or claiming fleet capacity.

contracts.question: What evidence supports production release and fleet-scale capacity claims?
contracts.decision: Require behaviorally equivalent application workloads, security/fuzz/chaos evidence and controlled repeated measurements.

contracts.question: Which legacy Blok v2 workflow subset can be structurally converted and exported without changing business behavior?
contracts.decision: ADR 0019 defines a bounded structural-only subset, pinned node inventory, strict duplicate/unknown-field handling, actionable rejection, and exact representable Export rules. Startup, idle, load and recovery distributions plus independent Review R remain open for E20-T01.

contracts.question: What must every trigger adapter declare and prove, and how does an extension author check it?
contracts.decision: Adapters publish a validated completion/disconnect/authentication Declaration, dispatch through an injected handler without interpreting or retrying, and pass contract/conformance.RunTrigger plus import-graph checks (ADR 0005).

contracts.question: How does an adapter hand verified work to durable admission and acknowledge only after commit?
contracts.decision: trigger.Submitter commits a keyed submission with its principal before returning; duplicates are reported, conflicts refused. worker.Queue implements it; webhooks acknowledge only after it returns (ADR 0006).

contracts.question: When does a broker message become Blok's, and who retries it?
contracts.decision: The consumer acknowledges the broker only after durable submission commits under a stable message key; execution retries belong to the queue, poison messages are dead-lettered before termination, and broker flow control bounds in-flight work (ADR 0007).

contracts.question: What happens to identity, ordering and slow or lost peers on a WebSocket connection?
contracts.decision: The server assigns connection identity; each connection runs one message at a time with a bounded queue; floods, slow readers and missed pongs close the connection with declared codes; OnDisconnect runs exactly once (ADR 0008).

contracts.question: What is a cron occurrence across DST, clock shifts, downtime and restarts?
contracts.decision: An occurrence is its UTC instant under explicit gap/fold policies, submitted under a stable key before a never-backwards cursor is written; catch-up and overlap are bounded policies and one goroutine drives every schedule (ADR 0009).

contracts.question: What does an SSE subscriber see across reconnects, restarts, slow reads and authorization, and what survives a disconnect?
contracts.decision: A start is a durable submission keyed by caller and idempotency key; its progress is best-effort, bounded and in memory, with epoch-qualified event ids, explicit retention/restart gaps, disconnect of slow subscribers, authorization before any stream byte, and a separate synchronous audit path (ADR 0010).

contracts.question: How does a unary gRPC method map to a workflow, its errors and its bounds, and how does it share a server with the worker runtime?
contracts.decision: Generated method descriptors map to domain values by protojson, proven against the binding and workflow schemas at startup; calls are authenticated from metadata, authorized per method on the server, bounded in time, size and concurrency, answered with status codes carrying stable codes only; application services refuse the worker runtime's package and any name already registered (ADR 0013).

contracts.question: Which catalog tools can an MCP client see and call, as whom, and what stops an unreviewed effect, a hijacked session or abandoned work?
contracts.decision: Only tools the endpoint exposes by name@version, the catalog lists for the caller and whose schemas MCP can carry are visible; each call runs as the principal its own request authenticated, is schema-validated, bounded in concurrency and time, and dispatched through the catalog, where a named approval is only looked up; errors reach the model as stable codes; sessions and calls are bounded globally and per principal; a client cancel, a dropped request or the owner ending its session cancels the work (ADR 0014).

contracts.question: How are native run and step observations versioned, authorized, redacted, bounded and paginated?
contracts.decision: inspection/v1 exposes immutable app-composed Go and Node outcomes, a bounded process-local recorder, and a principal-authorized SQL journal read port for actual waits, attempts, uncertain effects and child lineage; payloads and blobs are separately bounded and redacted/authorized (ADR 0016).

contracts.question: How does a development reader follow a run live without being able to slow it, see what it may not, or miss a loss without knowing?
contracts.decision: An application-selected inspection observer feeds a bounded process-local hub (observe/event, standard library only) served as Server-Sent Events by inspect.NewEventHandler; publication never waits on a reader (a full queue disconnects it), capture of inputs/outputs/logs is off by default and policy-gated per reader, every loss is an in-sequence or cursor-derived gap, late worker logs are followed for a bounded window after the terminal frame, every connection is admitted against reader limits before any replay or durable read, and a run without live history is reconstructed from the journal as the reader and followed live only under its durable owner, within a per-principal recovered budget that never evicts live runs (ADR 0016).
